original.description: The objective of this activity is to design, implement and evaluate different types of satellite system architectural models aimed at dynamically focusing available resources on coverage gaps in terrestrial 4G and 5G networks.Targeted Improvements:Achieving national regulator coverage and service objectives for direct-to-device services and enabling twice as efficient satellite resourcespooling over the service area.Description: Today there are coverage gaps of the terrestrial telecommunication system despite initiatives from non-European industries to provide supplementary coverage from space. Concentrating satellite connectivity exclusively on coverage gap areas (including low service areas) rather than aiming for satellite connectivity over a broad coverage has the potential to maximize the efficiency of the satellite system. It could offer an increased throughput which translates in reduced deployment costs per bit and higher quality of service for end users. Moreover, this approach could enable flexible resources allocation based on the population density as well as step up and step down of terrestrial connectivity services.This activity will design,implement and evaluate satellite system architectural models addressing non-uniform spatiotemporal traffic patterns in particular of handheld services. First, the activity will develop a high-resolution spatiotemporal traffic model, which shall consider available datasets and trend analyses of service requirements of Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) and their representative organisations, along with actual and target service coverage obligation set by National Regulation Administrations (NRAs) for terrestrial network gaps. The outputs of this model will be used to define coverage gaps from existing and planned terrestrial networks and space networks. The activity will then study and implement in a software prototype Distributed Satellite System (DSS) concepts for Frequency Range 1 (FR1) considering different orbits, multi-connectivity techniques (e.g. beam overlapping, coordinated multi-point etc) and infrastructure configurations (e.g. fractionated, swarm and federated concepts). System sizing optimizing the satellite resources will be carried out of at least 3 selected DSS concepts and the performance will be evaluated by simulation. The activity shall identify the most promising DSS concept and development roadmap considering complexity and system performance and the ability to accommodateopportunities beyond direct to device services. original.description: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time. However, existing data are limited, fragmented and often unsuitable for consistent spacecraft-level brightness analyses. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a system-integrated European database of optical properties for spacecraft materials with potential observational impacts, including solar arrays, multilayer insulation, thermo-optical coatings, antennas and external optical elements. The activity shall establish the required material datasets, perform dedicated measurement and characterisationcampaigns, and integrate the resulting data into an open-access database supporting DQS compliance assessments and brightness prediction tools. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 7.

original.description: Objective: To model the hypersonic flow around critical points of the re-entry of a upper stage vehicle, accounting for the catalytic properties of a Si-O-C ceramics, and for the chemical modifications of the surface exposed to the air.Description: There is a renewed interest in the implementation of reusable vehicles for in-orbit operation. A critical aspect in the lifetime of a space vehicle is to improve the durability of the thermal protection structures, to limit the replacement of the thermal shield. Ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTC) materials, based on the Si-O-C compounds with dedicated coatings (boride, molybdenum etc.) demonstrated to be a good choice, due to their capability to resist and survive above 1500 K. To fully evaluate the response of any material in suchextreme operating conditions, it is also imperative to determine the catalysis in high temperature gas, strongly affecting the surface heat flux. Moreover, the interaction of the material coatings with dissociated gases such as oxygen and nitrogen, induces variations on the material properties. The technology to be developed is to model accurately the complex physical processes at the gas surface interface during ascent and descent, in which different coatings are experimental tested validating the predictive capabilitiesof the numerical models. The model will include advanced kinetics, using a hybrid state-to-state -Multi-Temperature (StS-MT) derived from the StS, where the vibrational degrees of freedom are described by the vibrational temperature, while electronic excited states are treated as independent species, in order to estimate the radiative properties. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development of a chemical model of air interacting with the Si-O-C ceramic material, in dissociation regime; - Development of a hybrid StS-MT kinetic model - Develop a database for thermodynamic properties and of transport cross sections for air including Si-O-C species - Implementation of kinetics and transport in a numerical tool for hypersonic flows for the reliable simulation, flat plate/coupons - Model chemical gas surface interaction, chemical stability, roughness, thickness, stability of coatings, catalyst by experimental plasma testing of different samples, thermal optical properties, emission spectroscopy - Numerical modelling and testing thermal bounding of the silica based substrate bounding with the coating, testing of the attachment devices - Evaluation of differentceramics suitable for the orbital entry conditions.

original.description: Objective: To develop a comprehensive set of rigorously tested tools that ensures monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance for close proximity operations.Description: Past activities related to Close Proximity Operations (CPO) highlighted the need ofdeveloping low impact velocity tools that can verify and validate that the servicer spacecraft (SC) maintains a collision risk probability of less than given threshold (e.g 10^-4) with the client SC during CPO. For missions involving multiple SC in close formation, the design of manoeuvres to avoid collisions with catalogue objects not belonging to the formation requires to take into account all SC of the formation, e.g. an avoidance manoeuvre performed by one SC of the formation shall not trigger an inner-formation collision risk but rather minimise disturbance to the formation while ensuring the required risk reduction. This activity aims at developing a comprehensive set of tools (e.g. DRAMA like tool, prototype software for formation flying) that ensure monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance during close proximity operations (including formation flying). This activity encompasses the followingtasks: - Develop and refine software tools that model the trajectory of both the target and servicer. - Develop algorithms that identify safe trajectories for close approaches and include collision avoidance features. - Develop tools that perform uncertainty propagation to estimate the likelihood of a collision between the servicer and client. - Identify sensor systems capable of providing design and operational level data about the relative positions, velocities, and orientations of both the servicer and the target. - Conduct virtual testing within the developed tools to simulate close approach and rendezvous operations in various scenarios. - Develop mathematical models of constraints and requirements and prototype a software solution suitable for realistic scenarios.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a 5G NTN dual active modem prototype with active resource management for improving link reliability and performance, whileoptimizing the space segment resources utilization.TargetedImprovements:-doubling the peak data rate compared to state of art modems.- reduction by half link outage time.Description: The need for a dual-active modem in 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) arises from the growing demand for reliable, high-performance communication links particularly inscenarios where terrestrial networks are unavailable or unreliable. A dual-active NTN modem can maintain two simultaneous satellite links, significantly reducing the risk ofoutages caused by shadowing, fading or interference. At the same time, it provides an additional communication channel that enables load balancing across space segmentnodes, helping to distribute traffic efficiently and improve peak user data rates. Active resource management is essential in this context. Strategies must be designed todynamically allocate resources based on real-time link conditions and performance metrics. These strategies should ensure that the satellite system can optimize keyperformance indicators, such as peak data rate and service availability, while minimizing the resources allocated to each link and network node (e.g. payloads). Developingcontrol plane methodologies is also a critical aspect of this solution. The control plane manages the signalling and control information required for the operation of thecommunication links. It enables the system to gather real-time measurements of links conditions, which are essential for making informed decisions about resource allocationand link management. These methodologies also provide mechanisms for communicating decisions to the network including satellites and user terminals ensuring that thesystem can adapt to changing conditions and maintain optimal performance.This activity will develop a prototype dual-active 5G modem, potentially based on open radio stacks, and implement a testbed to evaluate the prototype under realisticconditions. This testbed will include a channel emulator with multiple RF interfaces to emulate themultiple links. Channel performance as well as satellite system resourcesallocation will be tested for various operational scenarios, and both resource management methodologies and control plane techniques will be assessed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl.
